title: Autonomous Triage Playbook for LLM Quality Anomalies
author: Ravi Shah
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines an autonomous-first triage process for LLM quality anomalies that impact customer-facing traffic. It is intended for SREs, Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), and first-line support to reduce mean-time-to-detect (MTTD) and mean-time-to-resolve (MTTR) using automated detection, quick remediations, and a controlled escalation path. The goal is to keep customer-impacting sessions within our SLOs while minimizing manual intervention.

When to use this playbook:
- Model output quality regressions (semantic drift, hallucination spikes, or abrupt response truncation) detected by telemetry or reported by customers.
- Automated synthetic checks trip quality gates (see "Synthetic checks" section).
- Multiple customers show correlated reductions in evaluation scores, or high false-positive rates in reranking endpoints.

Ownership and roles:
- Primary owner: Customer Success (CSEs) — initial customer communication and impact validation.
- Secondary owner: Eng SRE — metrics triage, routing, and capacity-related checks.
- Escalation owner: Runtime/Serving Engineering — model rollout and kernel-level investigation.
- Communications lead: Customer Success Manager (CSM) — external comms and timeline updates.

SLOs and thresholds (product-impact):
| Metric | SLO | Alert threshold (auto) | Severity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Quality eval delta (customer prompt-set) | < 1.0 point drop | >= 1.5 point drop | Sev-2 |
| Synthetic pass rate (paraphrase tests) | >= 98% | <= 95% | Sev-2 |
| Customer-reported critical failures / hour | 0 | > 3 | Sev-1 |
| End-to-end median latency (critical path) | < 250 ms | > 400 ms | Sev-3 |

Preconditions and safeguards:
- This playbook assumes telemetry pipelines are healthy and ingestion latency < 2 minutes. If telemetry is lagging, follow the "Telemetry degraded" checklist in the related SRE runbook before proceeding.
- All automated actions have a 2-step safety check: 1) internal detection + 2) synthetic confirmation or customer report. Exceptions require on-call approval.

Synthetic checks (automated):
- Nightly and rolling synthetic suites run against every active model variant:
  1) Intent preservation (20 queries per domain)
  2) Hallucination probes (10 factual checks)
  3) Paraphrase consistency (50 paraphrase pairs)
  4) Tokenization integrity (edge-case input set)
- Synthetic checks use tenant-focused prompt-sets when available. Any tiered tenant with > 100k tokens/day has a private prompt-set.
- Synthetic alerting thresholds configured in the orchestration layer: two consecutive windows of failing checks (5 minutes apart) triggers an automated triage.

Autonomous triage flow (high-level):
1) Detection: anomaly is flagged by either synthetic suite or customer telemetry (first-line).
2) Rapid classification: an automation job runs a prioritized checklist (see "automated diagnostics").
3) Quick mitigation: if automation classifies the issue as a reversible configuration or routing problem, it runs a guarded remediation (auto-rollback window: 10 minutes).
4) Human review: CSE or SRE reviews automation outputs; if unresolved, escalate per matrix.
5) Post-incident: produce short RCA and update customer and internal artifacts.

Automated diagnostics (scripts run in parallel):
- Verify model variant and pinned version for affected tenant(s).
- Re-simulate customer prompt-set against last-known-good model snapshot (runtimes: local replay).
- Check KV-cache hit rates and delta from baseline (significant drops indicate cache eviction regressions).
- Validate routing policy: confirm requests are not being routed to fallback variant with different tokenization/quantization profile.
- Confirm recent rollout timeline: check deploy logs for canary failures or rollback events in the previous 60 minutes.
- Execute a small golden test of 5 deterministic prompts to validate tokenization and truncation behavior.

Guarded automatic remediations (only when checks pass safety gate):
- Re-route 5% -> 50% of affected traffic to last-known-good model variant (gradual in 5% increments with 2-minute observation).
- Clear tenant prefix cache for affected tenant (single-key clear followed by throttled rebuild).
- Temporarily disable experimental tokenization fallback for the tenant.
- Auto-rollback of the most recent model rollout if success rate < 80% in 10-minute window.

Automated remediation CLI examples:
- Re-route command (internal):
  redwood ctl routing set --tenant TENANT_ID --from VARIANT_B --to VARIANT_A --percent 20 --observe 120

- Rollback model rollout (internal):
  redwood ctl model rollback --model-id model-llama-13b-q4_1 --to-version v2028-01-22 --force --dry-run=false

Escalation matrix and timings:
- Sev-1 (customer-visible critical failure; >3 critical failures/hour or >5% eviction of customers): immediate page to on-call SRE and CSE; 15-minute bridge. Notify Eng Runtime within 30 minutes.
- Sev-2 (quality regression, synthetic fail): page CSE on-call; 60-minute bridge target. Invoke guarded remediation first.
- Sev-3 (degraded latency or single-tenant non-critical): ticket to SRE queue; 4-hour review.

Escalation contacts (examples):
- On-call SRE: PagerDuty schedule (primary/secondary)
- Runtime lead: runtime-oncall@redwood.internal
- Model Ops: modelops@redwood.internal

Customer communication templates (short):
- Initial acknowledgement (automated):
  "We have detected an issue affecting model responses for your tenant. Our systems have started an automated triage and we will follow up within 30 minutes with next steps. — Redwood Support"

- Follow-up (if mitigation in progress):
  "We've temporarily routed a portion of traffic to a stable model variant and are monitoring results. You may see transient differences in output format while we complete verification. We expect to confirm resolution within 60 minutes. — CSE"

Investigation checklist (human-driven):
1) Confirm customer context and recent actions (model pinning, prompt-set changes, schema changes).
2) Re-run synthetic prompt-set targeted to the tenant; compare token-level diffs.
3) Review recent deployments and canary logs. Note any kernel or CUDA errors.
4) Inspect backend logs for partial responses, aborted streams, or gRPC resets.
5) Validate KV-cache metrics and persistence store latency.
6) If applicable, request a sample conversation from the customer and replay it against known-good snapshot.

Telemetry assertions to collect during incident:
- eval.score.{tenant_id} (time-series)
- synthetic.passrate.{model_variant} (rolling 5m)
- kvcache.hit_rate.{tenant_id} and kvcache.evictions.{tenant_id}
- routing.swap_events.{tenant_id}
- model.deploy.duration.{model_id}

Post-incident actions and RCA template (deliverables):
- Short RCA (one-page): timeline, impact (tenants affected, duration), root cause, contributing factors, immediate remediation, and permanent fix owner + ETA.
- Customer summary (plain language) and compensation recommendation if needed per SLA.
- Update synthetic prompt-sets if gaps discovered; add new probes.
- Add automated checks or tighten thresholds where automation missed signal.

Permanent fixes matrix (examples):
| Problem class | Permanent fix | Owner | ETA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cache eviction surge | Increase per-tenant cache cap + eviction backpressure | Eng Runtime | 3 weeks |
| Tokenization mismatch after quantized rollout | Add tokenization regression tests in CI | Model Ops | 2 weeks |
| Undetected partial stream truncation | Add end-of-stream guard metric and alert | Eng SRE | 1 week |

Runbook review cadence and training:
- Quarterly playbook review with Eng Runtime, SRE, and CSEs.
- Annual game-day where automation is disabled for 2 full hours to validate human procedures.
- New CSE on-boarding: 90-minute hands-on lab using the synthetic harness and the simulated incident runner.

Appendix: quick check commands and sample queries
- Check recent deploy events:
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://deploys.redwood.internal/api/v1/events?model=model-llama-13b | jq '. | .[0:5]'

- Query synthetic pass rate (example PromQL):
  avg_over_time(synthetic_passrate{model_variant="prod-llama-13b"}[10m])

- Sample deterministic prompt to validate hallucination regression:
  "Q: Who is the current Secretary-General of the United Nations? A:"

Notes and provenance:
- This playbook consolidates lessons from customer incidents in 2026–2027 and the runtime kernel regressions in 2027. It favors an autonomous-first posture with human gates for customer-visible rollbacks.
- Related runbooks: eng-sre/runbooks/telemetry-degraded-checklist and eng-serving-runtime/release-notes/rollback-guidelines.
